name: Cho'Gath
notes: Opens with Feast (R) at t = 0 for its true-damage burst, then Rupture (Q) and Feral Scream (W) go out on cooldown; Vorpal Spikes (E) is cast right after an attack lands whenever it is off cooldown, using its own attack-timer reset, and its 3 charges are then consumed by the next 3 attacks; auto-attacks fill every other gap.
Feast's true damage uses the champion formula (base + 50% AP + 10% bonus health) since the dummy counts as an enemy champion; the separate non-champion/monster base (1200) is never used.

Assumes 0 permanent Feast stacks: nothing forces a pre-fight kill for a level-16 Cho'Gath entering this fight, so neither the extra bonus health, the wiki's +8/12/16-per-stack Feast damage, nor Vorpal Spikes' +0.5%-per-stack term are added; Vorpal Spikes' listed target-max-health percentages already are the 0-stack values.
Vorpal Spikes' target-max-health-% damage uses the champion (uncapped) formula, not the reduced monster cap, since the dummy counts as an enemy champion.

Rupture's damage is dealt on cast: the wiki's extra 0.625 s delay before the rupture lands (on top of the 0.5 s cast) is not modeled, the same way the reference driver treats a short cast-to-impact delay as instant.
Feral Scream's damage is likewise dealt on cast, even though it technically lands at cast-time end; both casts still take the engine's standard 0.25 s post-cast attack lockout.
Feast's 0.25 s cast time is covered by the same 0.25 s lockout; its damage is dealt on cast (the opening cast at t = 0 is primed and lockout-handled by the engine itself).
Carnivore (P) only triggers on a kill, which never happens against a stationary dummy with a large health pool, so it contributes nothing and is omitted.
Crowd control (the knock-up, the silence, both slows) is ignored, as instructed: none of it affects a stationary, non-attacking dummy.
Mana costs are not modeled: nothing here binds across a 15 s fight at level 16.
